summary: Where this page sits in the hierarchy, and how to get back up. An ordered list inside a named landmark.
useWhen: a page sits more than one level deep and the parent is not otherwise reachable
a record view needs its collection one click away
the hierarchy itself is information the user needs — which project, which environment

useInstead.when: the destinations are siblings rather than ancestors
useInstead.why: a breadcrumb describes depth; tabs describe alternatives at the same depth

useInstead.when: the trail is the primary navigation for the whole app
useInstead.why: a breadcrumb supplements navigation, it does not replace it — it appears after a user has already gone somewhere

children.note: ancestor first, current page last. Anything else and the trail reads backwards

requires: `label` when a page has more than one nav landmark — it defaults to "Breadcrumb", which is what screen-reader users listen for
notes: the separator is drawn by CSS ::before and never enters the accessibility tree; a "/" in the markup is announced as punctuation between every crumb
the list is an `ol`, so the position and length are announced — which is the entire content of a breadcrumb

antiPatterns.why: a row of divs conveys neither sequence nor position, and the slashes are read aloud

antiPatterns.dont: a full trail on a top-level page
antiPatterns.why: a breadcrumb with one crumb is furniture — it takes vertical space to say nothing
